This allows you to measure system performance, rate-limiting effectiveness, and lockout mechanisms without compromising actual user data.

#### 1. Use Synthetic Credentials
Never use real or leaked passwords. Generate random username/password pairs that do not exist in your production database. This ensures that any failed login attempts are harmless and do not trigger real account lockouts or alert real users.

#### 2. Isolate the Test Environment
Run tests against a staging or development environment that mirrors production but is disconnected from real user data. This prevents accidental impact on live services.

#### 3. Implement Rate Limiting and Lockout Tests
The goal of such a test is to verify that your security controls work. You should configure your test to intentionally trigger rate limits and account lockouts to ensure they function as expected.
